morphology.motility: Non-motile — distinguishes Shigella from most other Enterobacterales

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human intestinal tract only — no significant animal reservoir
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Survives in contaminated water/food; very low infectious dose

culture.colonyMorphology: Colorless (non-lactose fermenting) colonies on MacConkey; no H2S production, unlike Salmonella, on XLD

identificationClues: Non-motile — a key feature distinguishing it from most other Enterobacterales, including Salmonella
H2S negative on XLD/TSI, unlike most Salmonella
Very low infectious dose (as few as 10-100 organisms)

diseases: Shigellosis (bacillary dysentery) — fever, abdominal cramps, bloody mucoid diarrhea
virulenceFactors: Shiga toxin (potent in S. dysenteriae, present at lower levels in other species)
Invasion plasmid antigens allowing invasion of colonic epithelium
Very low infectious dose enabling person-to-person spread
clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral, including person-to-person spread (due to the very low infectious dose), contaminated food/water
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A common cause of bacillary dysentery worldwide, with a disproportionate burden in young children in areas with limited sanitation; outbreaks also occur in daycare and close-contact settings in higher-resource countries
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Non-motility plus non-lactose fermentation plus H2S-negative TSI reaction together distinguish it from the closely related, H2S-positive Salmonella on routine stool culture media

examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Non-motile and H2S-negative, unlike the biochemically similar but H2S-positive, motile Salmonella
